rule: A pass is a commit that produced a new board state (a routing or placement change to a hw/*.kicad_pcb file). Passes are numbered sequentially in commit order; pass 1 is the first committed board state. Runs whose boards were never committed are not numbered — they are listed under gaps. Strategy changes live in each entry's description (the changelog), never in the numbering.

passes.description: Placement only: 144 footprints placed, GND zones and the HV isolation slot drawn, saved unrouted — the routing run was interrupted by a VM replacement. First committed board state; 0 of 112 nets routed.
passes.note: Snapshot renders were made later from the board as committed at d0c0bca.

passes.description: First committed routed board. Router gains neck-down where wide tracks meet fine-pitch pads and power-first net ordering (HV > power > LVDS > signals) — the fixes for the uncommitted v1/v2 failures (see gaps). 57 of 112 nets fully routed, 90 pins failed; no audit file was committed with this pass, so clearance violations and unconnected nets are not recorded.

Goal-cell exemption fix: a net's own target cells no longer count as blocked for it. 67 of 112 nets fully routed, 59 pins failed. The clearance figure (454) is the audit's violating-pair count as recorded in commit f8b9d1c — no audit file was committed with the pass itself — and the unconnected-net count was not recorded.

Stricter clearance model in the router: vias never exempt, segment-midpoint tests, layer-aware HV clearance. Traded connections for correctness — 58 of 112 nets fully routed, 74 pins failed. First pass with a full audit committed: 98 unconnected nets, 341 clearance violations.

Repair pass over the pass-4 board — the first repair run to survive to a commit (attempts 1–3 were lost; see gaps). 82 isolated groups connected across 2 sweeps, but clearance violations rose 341 → 445, so it was NOT adopted as the main board; the board is kept as the attempt artifact. Its verdict drove the next rewrite: the router's clearance model (grid-node + segment-midpoint tests) systematically under-protects against the audit's exact shape geometry.
passes.note: Audit: results/audit-repair-attempt4.txt, committed with the pass (copper items 2,208). No renders were committed for this pass.

passes.description: Router rewritten with an exact clearance model — per-segment shape-distance tests in blocked(), zero slack, parity with the audit — and run full-board from the placed board: 30 of 112 nets fully routed, 144 pins failed, 83 unconnected nets, 64 clearance violations, none of them involving router-emitted geometry (46 known placement pad pairs + 18 zone-involved). Model proven; connectivity is what remains. Adopted as the main board.

Repair over the pass-6 board, with two-segment fanout escapes for pads sitting on grid boundaries: 45 groups connected, unconnected nets 83 → 62, clearance violations unchanged at 64. Board kept as hw/pdlvds_rx.repaired6.kicad_pcb.
passes.note: Audit: results/audit-repair6-attempt1.txt, committed with the pass (copper items 2,115). Pins-failed is recorded as not recorded: no figure exists in this pass's own records (the old gallery index carried 74, parsed from a stale build log, not from this pass).

passes.description: Bundled change — two strategy changes in a single commit, the practice this counter replaces: diagonal moves added to the repair router AND the repair re-run over the pass-7 board. Result: 0 groups connected, no progress, not adopted. The commit's real payload is the per-pin diagnosis of the residue (results/diagnose-repaired6b.txt): of 99 isolated groups, 50 NO_EXIT, 16 POCKET, 20 WIDE_NO_GOAL, 13 REACHES — pads boxed in by placement, which is what pass 9 changes.
passes.note: Board saved as hw/pdlvds_rx.repaired6b.kicad_pcb (1,587 tracks per results/repair6-attempt2.log). No audit was committed for this pass, so unconnected nets and clearance violations are not recorded. No renders were committed.

passes.description: Placement change, answering pass 8's diagnosis: the U7/U12/L2/X1 cluster is moved on the pass-7 board to unbox pads that had no exit — 24 pad pairs removed, 0 added. Board saved as hw/pdlvds_rx.moved.kicad_pcb.
passes.note: Audit: results/audit-moved.txt, committed with the pass (copper items 1,392). No renders were committed for this pass.

passes.description: Repair resumed over the placement-revised board (pass 9) and — the first pass committed under the sharpened rule — committed at checkpoint 1 of the run instead of at run end: 111 groups connected, unconnected nets 69 → 49. The audit committed with the checkpoint reads 1,435 clearance violations on 3,424 copper items; checkpoint saves did not refill zones at the time (fixed in cabbebc), and the figure is recorded exactly as the committed audit states it — a mid-run checkpoint state, not a finished-board audit. The run was still in progress when this was committed.
passes.note: Audit: results/audit-repair6-attempt3-ckpt1.txt, committed with the pass. Pins-failed not recorded (the old gallery index's 74 came from the same stale build-log parse as pass 7's). The 1,435 clearance violations in this pass's audit are a stale-zone-fill artifact of mid-run checkpoint saves (zones refilled only at run end, so the input board's stored pours were counted against new copper); fixed structurally in cabbebc — zones now refill at every checkpoint save. The comparable post-refill violation count for this board state is 64.

passes.description: placement relief: J2 shifted -4 mm in x (pads 5/6 were 2.08 mm outside the outline); 40 audit-driven nudges (hw/relief_nudge.py) clear all 22 inter-part pad clearance violations, several at gap 0.000 (touching); only small passives moved, no ICs, APD/TIA cluster untouched; remaining audit items = 20 INTRINSIC same-footprint pairs + 56 stale zone-fill pairs (refilled at route import); unrouted, Freerouting next

Freerouting v2.5.0 routes the pass-11 relief placement (6 passes, score plateau ~221, best state kept: 148/402 connections unrouted by FR); SES imported via hw/import_ses.py after fixing its unit scaling (SES is in 0.1 um resolution units, importer assumed um and landed at 10x; fix parses (resolution um N)); importer also refills zones. Audit: 44 unconnected nets (power nets dominate: +3V3D 20 groups, +5V 15, +3V3A 13, GND 10), 13 clearance items all one family (APD_K pads/tracks vs F.Cu GND pour, 1.0 mm HV rule), 20 intrinsic; repair6 in checkpointed runs next

repair6 checkpoint 1 on the Freerouting board (pass 12): 10 groups connected in the first ~90 s of sweep 1 (contrast: 0 in 90 min on the pre-relief placement); run continues checkpointing on hw/pdlvds_rx.fr1r.kicad_pcb

gaps.label: router v1 run (commit dc6a010, 2026-11-03T19:39:29Z)
gaps.note: Board routed in memory only; the commit carries router code, no board. Its 125 failed pins are known only from later commit messages (passes 2–3). Not numbered.

gaps.label: router v2 run (commit c79defe, 2026-11-03T20:10:21Z)
gaps.note: Wide-nets-first ordering; board never committed and no result tally recorded. Not numbered.

gaps.label: repair attempts 1–3 over the pass-4 board (commits 2add453, 0c20958, 04c90b4)
gaps.note: Attempt 1's board was lost at save; attempt 2 connected 82 groups in memory, then crashed at the same save (variable `path` shadowing the board path — root cause proven in 0c20958, which also retro-explains attempt 1); attempt 3 was killed by a VM replacement mid-sweep (04c90b4). The commits carry code and logs but no board. Pass 5 is repair attempt 4, the first to be committed. Not numbered.

gaps.label: in-flight run state lost to a VM replacement (commit 8d39045)
gaps.note: Both /tmp scratch trees (v6 routing and the Freerouting line), with their logs and checkpoints, were lost; any board states in them were never committed. Scratch state moved into the workspace afterwards. Not numbered.

gaps.label: Freerouting baseline line
gaps.note: No board produced by Freerouting has ever been committed (the native CLI build is dead — 8d39045; the JVM/AppImage line produced no committed board either), so it holds no pass numbers. If it ever produces a committed board state, it takes the next number like everything else.
